newsitem.title: USA: Fla. police officer shot hours after riot ruling.
newsitem.headline: Fla. police officer shot hours after riot ruling.

text.p: An officer was shot and police used tear gas to break up crowds of youths on Wednesday, hours after a Florida grand jury ruled that a white officer was justified in shooting a black motorist whose death sparked a night of rioting, police said.

An unidentified male officer was shot in the leg after police responded to a report of gunfire in south St. Petersburg, a predominantly black section of the city rocked by rioting on Oct. 24, St. Petersburg police spokesman Bill Doniel said.
Officers responding to the reported gunfire were subjected to rock and bottle throwing and then shots were fired, one of them striking the officer in the left leg, Doniel said.
Police used tear gas to break up small bands of youths roaming the streets, he said.
Another officer, Maj. Cedric Gordon, told reporters that the wounded officer was "doing fine."

Police had stepped up patrols in the neighbourhood after a grand jury ruled that Officer James Knight was justified in shooting motorist Tyron Lewis following a routine traffic stop. Following the ruling, Knight was suspended by the police department for 60 days without pay for violating its firearms policy.
